limitations: Diagnostic profiling may overlap compiler builds and tests pinned away from CPU5; these are not acceptance timings.
Function CPU attribution uses exclusive samples; inclusive helper/call durations must not be added.
JIT labels contain local slot names and a code address, not JavaScript function names; source names are joined to retained origin metadata.
One diagnostic process per selected component, including startup, warmup, timed work and final collection; not a full-suite profile.
CPU proportions use a separate map-disabled process to avoid source-map stderr work; source-name joins by label/code size are explicitly marked exact, approximate or ambiguous.
Nearest template-family PC attribution is reported only from the exact-address map-enabled process. No PC offsets are transferred to code versions whose emitted sizes differ.
A one-millisecond interval and one run give descriptive profile proportions, not confidence intervals or throughput acceptance.
Generic allocator/hash symbols are grouped by symbol family; their compilation/GC/runtime caller population is not separated.

Nearest emission markers span fused regions and may name their final bytecode rather than the instruction actually sampled. They are raw navigation hints, not accurate opcode cost buckets; in particular region:Jump does not establish branch cost.
